hook: SCP-2021 is a short, quiet file about a box of copy paper in which every sheet has only one real side. It reads like a tidy lab report covering three small experiments, and the unease comes from details mentioned almost in passing. Don't skim the two addenda at the end.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of an everyday-object anomaly that stays small in scale yet leaves a lingering wrongness. The file never explains what lies past the paper, and it doesn't need to; the experiments are arranged so that the reader puts the implications together. The handwritten label on the box hints at a previous owner without ever following that thread.
thingsToNotice: The reverse side behaves like an opening: a hamster disappears beneath it and comes back, a person standing behind it sees straight through, and a beaker pulled out through it leaves the original beaker sitting untouched on the table. What stays with you is the aftermath, as the D-class's right arm now feels like someone else's and can't identify objects by touch, and Dr. Marlowe reports the same thing in two fingertips. The sheet that slipped face-down before the tests was never recovered, and weeks later the test chamber has a smell of decay that two cleanings can't remove; the article sets those facts side by side and leaves them unconnected.
